source_evidence.observation: Display (2.8) states that if X has the Poisson distribution with parameter lambda, then for every t greater than lambda, P{X >= t} is at most exp(-lambda) times (e lambda / t)^t.

source_evidence.anchor: Exercise 2.3.3 heading, lead-in, and hint surrounding display (2.8)
source_evidence.observation: The display is the conclusion of Exercise 2.3.3, and the hint says to combine Chernoff's inequality with the Poisson limit theorem, Theorem 1.3.4.

binders: A Poisson random variable X with parameter lambda.
A threshold t ranging over real values comparable with lambda.
definitions_and_conventions: Pois(lambda) denotes the Poisson distribution with parameter lambda.
P{X >= t} is the probability of the inclusive upper-tail event.
The real threshold t also appears as the exponent in (e * lambda / t)^t.
implicit_context: Display (2.8) is not a freestanding claim: it inherits X ~ Pois(lambda) and t > lambda from the immediately enclosing Exercise 2.3.3.
The result occurs in Section 2.3, Chernoff's inequality.
The source relies on the standard admissible parameter convention for Pois(lambda); the local exercise does not restate that domain.
The hint's reference to Theorem 1.3.4 specifies a proof route, not another component of the displayed conclusion.

details: The displayed inequality must be read with both hypotheses supplied by the preceding sentence of Exercise 2.3.3.
The equation label (2.8) identifies the same Poisson upper-tail claim as the exercise, not an independent unconditional inequality.
The distributional hypothesis fixes the law of X to Pois(lambda).
The probability is for the inclusive event X >= t.
lambda is the Poisson rate/mean parameter.
t is an upper-tail threshold and satisfies the strict condition t > lambda.
The right-hand side is exp(-lambda) multiplied by (e * lambda / t)^t.
The same t occurs in the comparison event, the denominator, and the exponent.

undebatable_constraints: The enclosing hypothesis X ~ Pois(lambda) is part of the meaning of display (2.8).
The enclosing condition t > lambda is part of the meaning of display (2.8).
The event is the inclusive upper tail {X >= t}.
The inequality is non-strict and is an upper bound on that probability.
The displayed right-hand side is exactly exp(-lambda) * (e * lambda / t)^t.
The equation label contributes no extra hypotheses or conclusions beyond its enclosing exercise.

ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 8; printed page 19 introduces only 'X ~ Pois(lambda)' before display (2.8), without saying locally whether lambda = 0 is allowed.
ambiguities.impact: A formal version must choose whether the degenerate zero-rate Poisson law lies in scope.

ambiguities.issue: The source does not explicitly type the threshold t.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 8; printed page 19 says 'for any t > lambda' and display (2.8) uses t as a threshold and exponent.
ambiguities.impact: The notation supports a real threshold, while an integer-only formal statement would reduce applicability.

contract_plain_english: With the hypotheses inherited from Exercise 2.3.3, display (2.8) says: if X has Poisson law Pois(lambda), then for every threshold t strictly greater than lambda, P(X >= t) <= exp(-lambda) (e lambda / t)^t. The display is the exercise's exact conclusion; its Poisson-parameter convention and the type of t are implicit in the printed passage.
